Permit API: 003-22166
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Glenfield Borough

Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of this well on 7/25/2024. The well remained in the same condition as the previous inspection in 11/2023. The well was equipped to produce gas, and the valves remained open. The Operator has failed to comply with the conditions set forth in the Order and is therefore in violation of OGA3259(1).

Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "SGL12 L South" Marcellus well site.Chesapeake finished hydraulically fracturing the 3 Marcellus wells here in October 2022.Tony Savitski (Chesapeake) called the DEP on Monday January 16, 2023 (yesterday) to report an estimated 20 gallon spill of produced liquid from a vac truck to the pad surface. Chesapeake removed the visually impacted pad material and staged it on liner containment on the north corner of the pad. That material returned a >4.00 mS/cm electrical conductivity (EC) reading. I spoke with Andy Steffe and Ryan Carmody (both Creston Environmental) on site. They are screening the excavated area near the production tank for EC with a Hanna Groline Soil Test soil probe. I used the same model soil probe in the excavated area also. Both meters maxed out (>4.00 mS/cm), indicating residual production liquid impact from the spill yesterday morning. Background pad material gave 0.07-0.19 mS/cm readings. Creston is collecting solid samples from the excavated area, and from the waste material on the liner.Violations for the produced liquid spill are cited to the 015-23622 well permit.Mountain Energy is cleaning out the 9 wheelie trailers that the 3 Marcellus wells were flowing back into.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.16-0.74 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS 5.Air temp 36FJLP

Comments: On December 13, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline, John Ciccone, and Amber Boyd conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. At the time of inspection, the recently stimulated wells were in flow back. This inspection is to follow up with the multiple spills at this site. About half of the containment from the recent stimulation process has been removed. With the removal of some of the containment STL was able to excavate the area of elevated conductivity off the east end of the containment found on October 24, 2022. The area of excavation was about 90 ft. x 45 ft. and about 8 to 12 inches deep. The second area of elevated conductivity has been excavated to the containment. Containment remains in this area for the flow back process. Soil conductivity could not be screened in either of the excavated areas due to the ground being frozen.The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. Seep 3 was not able to be screened with the conductivity meter due to the lack of water at the seep. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 90.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.6 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, 3445592, and 3467217.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8208982
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/21/2024
Comments: On 11/21/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alterations inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 36 degrees and partly cloudy when I arrived on location. Rainfall had impacted the region in the past 24 hours.Inspecting the original Taft 851 1V pad, I did witness a secondary containment structure containing drilling mats with water at the level of the containment wall and fluid from the containment on the unprotected ground (picture 5). The water field tested at 0.301 mS conductance. Seneca's Jeff Passerrello was notified and was scheduling to have the containment emptied.Anthony Murphy described current operations as follows: A Nextier frac fleet has finished completion operations on five new wells at the site. Two snubbing/well servicing units were on site, drilling plugs out of the five completed wells. The units were on the first two wells and Anthony expects it to take a week to drill plugs on each well. He expects the crews to finish drilling plugs on all five wells by 12/10/2024. Anthony accompanied me on the site inspection. All operations were being conducted within a plastic lined containment structure that was protected by drilling mats. I did witness frac tanks, gas buster tanks, vac boxes and various chemical totes staged in secondary containment. There were ten frac tanks with fresh and produced water, six gas busters, and eight vac boxes staged near the snubbing/servicing units all staged in secondary containment. 28 frac tanks were staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. I did witness water in the transfer manifold duck pond on the west side of the snubbing units that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance. Anthony will have the liquids removed.During the inspection, I did witness a 5' x 8' water puddle near the north-central pad outfall that field tested at 19.99 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-145. The upper conductivity limit of the Oakton PCTS5 is 19.99 mS. Water discharging from the north-central pad outfall into the sediment basin field tested at 19.99 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-146 and soil sample 9551-147. Water in the basin near the northeast overflow field tested at 3.07 mS conductance; I collected water sample 9551-148. Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berm 3 and the sedimentation basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. As recommended in the inspections listed above, the DEP continues to recommend pursuing Act 2 for the large amount of elevated conductance fluids discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin.The DEP recommends the following: 1. Remove the elevated conductance fluids and contaminated soils from the pad surface and the sediment basin.2. Continuously monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered.3. Monitor secondary containment structures for contaminants, for liquid levels and for adequate freeboard levels; remove liquids as necessary.I left the site at 1300 hours.

Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign containing the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on a stake near the well. The GPS coordinate on file for this well was verified as part of this inspection. Upon arrival to the site, it was evident that crude oil had recently leaked from a faulty stuffing box on this well. The discharged crude oil migrated onto the well site, then traveled linearly approximately 450 feet downslope of the well on the access road. The crude oil remained contained on the road surface and ultimately accumulated in a puddle of standing water at the bottom of the hill (see Photo 2). It is estimated that less than 1 barrel of crude oil has been released as part of this incident. No waterways have been affected from the event.A representative from Bull Run Resources, JR McLaughlin, was contacted in response to the event. He arrived to the site immediately to address the noted concerns. The leaking stuffing box was repaired and diapers were used to absorb the crude oil from the road surface and around the well head. Given there is no ongoing discharge and a bulk of the released product has been remediated, the violations associated with this incident are considered corrected.A future inspection will be conducted to ensure that the initial remediation efforts were sufficient.

Comments: On 06/03/2026 at 0017 hours the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a notification of a release at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County (CTS #398207). Representative Ralph Babcock stated "on 6/2/26 at 5:15 p.m., a Keystone Clear Water truck driver was loading production water when the line split releasing 25 gallons of produced water. Approximately 10 gallons of produced water spilled into a containment structure while the remaining 15 gallons of produced water spilled onto the ground. Keystone Clearwater vacuumed produced water from the containment structure and scraped up impacted soil for later disposal.The DEP contacted Repsol and spoke with Mr. Babcock at 1145 hours. He stated the material from the release had been recovered and placed in drums onsite. He stated the release took place in the off-loading area of the pad. He stated he was notified of the released at 2345 hours (06/02).On 06/04/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection. I arrived at 0915 hours and met with Mr. Babcock. Environmental Resources was onsite to collect samples from the release and the prior release (CTS#396090). The area of the release was ~33 feet long (photo #2). There were no pooled fluids in the area of the release. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 452-1042 us/cm. The cause of the release was due to a valve malfunction (photo #3). Environmental resources screened the soil in the area of the release and received readings of 1-1.3 mS/cm (1000-1300 us/cm). The recovered material was observed in drums onsite and held within secondary containment (photo #4).The DEP screened the area of the prior release (CTS #396090). Fluids within the stormwater ditch at the release point were field measured for EC at ~452 us/cm. Mr. Babcock stated that this week there would be more material removed from the stormwater ditch at the release point due to elevated soil readings. There was dead vegetation observed downgrade of the affected bio-retention basin (photo #15-16). Fluids within and directly upgrade of the furthest downgrade sump pump were measured for EC between 1.248-2.24 mS/cm (1248-2240 us/cm) (photo #17 and 18). Fluids downgrade of the sump pump were field measured for EC between 173.7-398 us/cm. The violations related to the recent spill (CTS #398207) are considered immediately corrected however, outstanding violations remain open for API#015-23994 from the previous release (CTS #396090).I departed at 1120 hours.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.
Violation ID: 8183691
Permit API: 129-28483
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Sewickley Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/16/2024
Comments: On April 16th, 2024 the Department conducted a routine inspection of EQT's Cook Well Pad located in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Accompanying in today's inspection is Samantha Foulk (WQSS DEP).At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was present at the entrance of the access road and the ERP was present in the onsite mailbox.There are 2 total wells on this well pad that appeared to be equipped for production and are surrounded by cement barriers. Well 17H's well tag as present at the time of inspection with all necessary information posted and no fluid discharges were observed from/near the wellhead. The 17H GPU was surrounded by cement barriers but was not in secondary containment. Well 17H has a SPUD date prior to the October 2016 promulgation of Chapter 78a, therefore secondary containment is not required to be installed. Staining of the gravel below the piping of the 17H GPU was observed. Soil conductivity readings were taken at the edge of the well site along the chainlink fence (0.186 mS) as a background, and then three others were taken at the base of the GPU piping where the discoloration can be seen (0.021 mS, 0.002 mS and 0.013 mS). These readings were comparable to the background and therefore are not indicative of a release.The 17H production tank was in secondary containment that had fluid pooled in it and was surrounded by cement barriers. A conductivity reading of the fluid within was 0.158 mS. The production tank appeared to be sound with no observable leaks or discharge. The Department recommends the Operator monitor the secondary containment to ensure that the fluid currently in it will not inhibit its 110% hold capacity requirements.The access road and well pad appeared to be stabilized. Upon inspection of the perimeter of the well site, at least 70% vegetative growth was seen throughout as well as two riprap aprons. The riprap apron at the front of the well site did not show any erosion or sedimentation concerns, however the riprap apron at the rear of the well site did exhibit concerns. The rear riprap apron appeared to be improperly implemented and/or maintained to adequately prevent channelized flow from forming. Approximately 45-50 feet of channelized flow containing sediment was observed going from the end of the riprap apron outlet to an agricultural field nearby. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the riprap apron outlet to prevent any further erosion from occurring. With the exception of this area of concern, the remainder of the well site appeared to exhibit greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth.Based on todays inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to maintain PCSM BMPs.Prior to leaving the location, the Department notified Operator representative Logan Dominick of the above-noted concern, who responded that they would promptly address it.

Comments: On 04/04/19 at approximately 1200 hours I conducted a routine complete inspection of the site. The Act 9 sign was in place. The site was gated and locked. The stream crossing over Lutz Run had been destroyed and was missing. Contrary to 105.172(a), Diversified failed to immediately notify the Department of the collapse of the crossing. Remaining culvert pipes were not properly maintained and sediment and debris were obstructing the flow of water through the structures. Materials used to construct the crossing had been washed downstream. Large stones from the crossing were present in the stream. The brine tanks were heavily corroded and had poor structural integrity. Multiple holes were observed in both brine tanks. Diversified failed to notify the Department of tank deficiencies within 3 days of discovery and failed to address and remedy the deficiencies contrary to 78A57(i). The Department requests 1 year (12 months) of brine tank inspections per 78A57(i) be provided to the Department. To achieve compliance the brine tanks must be replaced or remedied in accordance with manufacturer's specifications and applicable engineering design criteria. If the tanks are replaced adherence to chapter 78A regulations regarding secondary containment will be necessary. The Department requests 1 year (12 months) of periodic inspections of the crossing per 105.53 be provided to the Department. The Department requests Diversified provide the date the stream crossing was observed to be missing.

Violation ID: 8206532
Permit API: 125-29107
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: South Franklin Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/01/2024
Comments: On 11/01/2024 a Complaint Inspection was conducted at the Folly Hollow Farm Unit OG Well Pad in response to a suspected release reported by multiple landowners. PA DEP Oil and Gas Inspector Supervisor Scott Sabocheck and Range Resources Representatives, Barry Bugbee and Nick Reda were on site at the time of inspection.Conductivity probe calibrated on 11/01/2024.The following was observed during the inspection:-An area of staining was observed beneath a flare stack located off secondary containment. Mr. Bugbee indicated that fluid was released, in a mist, from the flare stack yesterday(10/31/24) between 8:30 and 9:00 am, that the quantity released was approximately 2 gallons, and that the impacted material, except for the portion beneath the flare stack, was removed immediately after the release. The area of removed material and stained material combined appeared to be approximately 10 ft long by 10 ft wide in an irregular shape. The Department requests clarification on how the quantity released was determined (Photo 1).-Field conductivity screening was conducted within the area of stained material around and beneath the flare stack. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 3.74 and 11.01 ms/cm (Photos 2-4).-Fluid was actively being released onto secondary containment during the plug removal from the well associated with the American Petroleum Institute (API) number 125-29107. Range Resources representative stated that the fluid released was fresh water (Photos 5-6).-Field conductivity screening was conducted within the area of fluid located in secondary containment. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 5.41 ms/cm and Over Range (OR), which equates to greater than 20 ms/cm (Photos 7-9).-During the inspection, the flare stack was broken down and removed and the impacted material was excavated. The pad aggregate was removed to a depth of approximately 1-3 inches. The final area of removed material measured approximately 10 ft long by 10 ft wide (Photos 10-11).-Post-remediation field conductivity screening was conducted. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 0.8 and 35.5 s/cm (Photos 12-15). Determination:Because the impacted material was removed and post-remediation screening values were below standard, violations of 78.57(a), 78a54, and SWMA 301 are being issued and immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: XPR RESOURCES LLC

Violation Date: 10/16/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8252371
Permit API: 129-28299
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/16/2025
Comments: On October 16 2025, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the Uschak 2 Well Pad and associated wells.The findings were as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that appeared to have all required information. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel, with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site appeared to exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.At the time of inspection, the well pad had 5 total wells, all of which appeared equipped for production. The well tag was present on the 1H well head at the time of this inspection. Upon inspection of the 1H well head, the Department observed fluid actively leaking from the well head. The fluid appeared to be leaking from the handwheel on the wellhead. Stained and saturated gravel was observed beneath the well head in an area about 1 foot in diameter. A conductivity reading was taken of the fluid from the source of the leak on the handwheel with a reading of 14.00mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the stained and saturated gravel below the wellhead with readings of 2.81mS, 2.30mS, 4.64mS, 5.25mS. These readings were elevated in comparison to the background reading of 0.20mS.Prior to leaving the site the Department spoke to operator representative Brad Campbell via phone call and informed him of the observed leak. Mr. Campbell stated they would assess and ensure the leak is fix/remediated.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Upon inspection of the additional production equipment onsite, the production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. There were no visible leaks with the GPU, and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a.OGI referral is being requested for further evaluation of the well head and the observed corrosion.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: On 2/14/20 an incident inspection of the Beacon well pad was conducted in response to a spill (CTS ID: 347983) reported on 2/10/20. The following was observed: >>On 2/11/20 WQSS John Carson spoke with Greylock Representative Keith Eighmey who reported that while drilling using a filming agent foam from an open topped tank blew to the well pad and via a failed seam in the pad containment traveled to the pad's drainage ditches and then to the primary sediment basin and into the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC; unnamed tributary to Frosty Run). The amount of material lost was reported as unknown but minimal. Operator sampling and MSDS were requested. >>At the time of inspection the sediment basin was found to be overflowing via the stand pipe resulting in substantial flow of sediment laden waters bypassing and flowing through site perimeter controls causing accelerated erosion and impact to the WOC. Additionally, the runoff stream and channel off site notably still bore multiple large piles of foam strongly indicating ongoing impact related to the reported spill. At the time of inspection dewatering/pumping out the impacted water from the sediment basin and appropriate disposal of the effluent as site waste was encouraged. Obstruction of the waterway was not approved. This spill and its impact constitutes a violation of 35 P.S. § 6018.301, 35 P.S. § 691.307(a), * 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, 25 Pa. Code § 91.34(a), 25 Pa. Code § 102.5(m)4, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e), 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1, 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)1, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.53 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. Violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e) and 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1 were related to the failure of site secondary containment and were shown to have been corrected by the operator prior to the time of inspection. >>A concurrent general surface inspection related to the site ESCGP (ESX16-059-0038) was conducted in response to observed site conditions, particularly multiple slope failures.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/25/2025
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8257125
Permit API: 081-21827
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/25/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that stated that on 11/24/25, an estimated 8 to 10 gallons of glycol was released to the pad surface. The notification also stated that the impacted pad material would be excavated with a mini-excavator and the material would be placed into barrels. Seven wells are staged for production on the well pad. Seven GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. No E and S issues noted.The area of the well pad impacted by the release had been excavated and the impacted material was placed into barrels on secondary containment prior to this inspection. A puddle of stormwater within the excavated area had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 154 uS/cm. Another puddle of stormwater in front of the production tanks had an EC of 532 uS/cm. Violations noted and are considered immediately corrected.
